description: Whether two programs are the same circuit up to a global phase, and how the engine knows: Clifford circuits by their tableaus at any size, others on every basis state to 8 qubits, then by checked rewrites of one followed by the other's inverse to nothing (a proof at any width), then on random product states to 22 (evidence, not proof), otherwise unchecked with the reason. Its `verdict` is that decision; `verification` is the level it reached, as every tool's verdict states it. A check that would take long here is refused with the command that runs it locally.
name: check_equivalent

anyOf.description: Whether two programs are the same circuit up to a global phase, and how the engine decided.

global_phase.description: The global phase between them, in units of π.

how.description: tableau, exact and rewrites are proofs; state is a proof of the same state from |0…0⟩; random is evidence, not proof; shape: they differ in their shape; none: unchecked.

steps.description: rewrites: the checked steps to nothing.

verification.description: How far the engine checked an answer about a program, as one level of an ordered ladder (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): refused, parsed, executed, evidence, proof. A level says how far the engine checked, not that the answer is good: holds says whether the intents held (true, false, or null when none was decided). A job's result carries one under verdict when the job gives an intent or asks for one, and the receipt seals it; both MCP servers state one beside every answer about a program.

critique.description: The program's smells, each with its lines.

executed.description: The method that ran and its accuracy class, and the distance a compile put between the program and what ran.

items.description: One intent's check: what it asked, whether it held, how strong the check was and how it was made.

distribution.description: The program's distribution, when its outcomes are few enough to list.

fit.description: A sampled intent: the test, its statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value, the level, and whether it rejected.

method.description: A sampled intent: the method the samples were run by.

outcomes.description: The outcomes the distribution holds, or the samples' distinct outcomes.

parsed.description: Whether the reader took the program, and its warnings and notes with their codes, or its refusal.

items.description: One of the reader's diagnostics: its code, what happens to the construct it is about, its message (without the line or the code), and where it stands.

text.description: The refusal as the reader wrote it, with its line and code.

rank.description: The level's place on the ladder, from 0 (refused) to 4 (proof).

refusal.description: For a refused job: its message and its codes.

repairs.description: Each edit a repair made, with the code it answered and the lines it changed.

statement.description: The level in one plain line.
